title: Act One. Purva-raga (First Attraction)
html:
Benediction and prologue: at the command of Gajapati Prataparudra the stage-director produces the drama of Ramananda Raya; Krishna enters Vrindavana with His jester-friend; hearing the flute, Radha comes to the grove with her friends; the first meeting of glances.

Verse 1

स्वराञ्चितविपञ्चिकामुरजवेणुसंगीतकं
त्रिभङ्गतनुवल्लरीवलितवल्गुहासोल्बणम् ।
वयस्यकरतालिकारणितनूपुरैरुज्ज्वलं
मुरारिनटनं सदा दिशतु शर्म लोकत्रये ॥ १ ॥

svarāñcitavipañcikāmurajaveṇusaṁgītakaṁ
tribhaṅgatanuvallarīvalitavalguhāsolbaṇam |
vayasyakaratālikāraṇitanūpurairujjvalaṁ
murārinaṭanaṁ sadā diśatu śarma lokatraye || 1 ||

svara-añcita — adorned with notes; vipañcikā — of the vina; muraja — of the muraja drum; veṇu — of the flute; saṅgītakam — accompanied by the music; tribhaṅga — bent in three places; tanu-vallarī — with the creeper of the body; valita — curved; valgu-hāsa-ulbaṇam — abounding in charming laughter; vayasya — of the friends; karatālikā — clapping of hands; raṇita-nūpuraiḥ — with jingling ankle-bells; ujjvalam — resplendent; murāri-naṭanam — the dance of Murāri; sadā — always; diśatu — may it bestow; śarma — happiness; loka-traye — in the three worlds.

1May the dance of Murari ever bestow happiness on the three worlds — accompanied by the music of the vina adorned with notes, the muraja drum and the flute; abounding in charming laughter as the creeper of His body bends in three places; resplendent with the clapping of His friends and the jingling of ankle-bells.1

Moreover:

Verse 2

स्मितं नु न सितद्युतिस्तरलमक्षि नाम्भोरुहं
श्रुतिर्न च जगज्जये मनसिजस्य मौर्वीलता ।
मुकुन्दमुखमण्डले रभसमुग्धगोपाङ्गना-
दृगञ्चलभवो भ्रमः शुभशताय ते कल्पताम् ॥ २ ॥

smitaṁ nu na sitadyutistaralamakṣi nāmbhoruhaṁ
śrutirna ca jagajjaye manasijasya maurvīlatā |
mukundamukhamaṇḍale rabhasamugdhagopāṅganā-
dṛgañcalabhavo bhramaḥ śubhaśatāya te kalpatām || 2 ||

smitam nu — is it a smile?; na — no; sita-dyutiḥ — the white-rayed (moon); taralam akṣi — a tremulous eye?; na — no; ambhoruham — a lotus; śrutiḥ — an ear?; na ca — nor; jagaj-jaye — for the conquest of the world; manasijasya — of the Mind-born (Kāma); maurvī-latā — the creeper of the bowstring; mukunda-mukha-maṇḍale — on the orb of Mukunda's face; rabhasa-mugdha — bewildered by eager joy; gopāṅganā — of the cowherd maidens; dṛg-añcala-bhavaḥ — arising in the corners of the eyes; bhramaḥ — this illusion; śubha-śatāya — for a hundred blessings; te — to you; kalpatām — may it serve.

2"Is it a smile? No — it is the white-rayed moon. A tremulous eye? No — a lotus. An ear? No — the bowstring with which the Mind-born conquers the world." May this illusion, born in the corners of the eyes of the cowherd maidens bewildered with eager joy at the orb of Mukunda's face, serve you for a hundred blessings.2

Moreover:

Verse 3

कामं कामपयोनिधिं मृगदृशामुद्भावयन्निर्भरं
चेतःकैरवकाननानि यमिनामत्यन्तमुल्लासयन् ।
रक्षःकोककुलानि शोकविकलान्येकान्तमाकल्पय-
न्नानन्दं वितनोतु वो मधुरिपोर्वक्त्रापदेशः शशी ॥ ३ ॥

kāmaṁ kāmapayonidhiṁ mṛgadṛśāmudbhāvayannirbharaṁ
cetaḥkairavakānanāni yamināmatyantamullāsayan |
rakṣaḥkokakulāni śokavikalānyekāntamākalpaya-
nnānandaṁ vitanotu vo madhuriporvaktrāpadeśaḥ śaśī || 3 ||

kāmam — abundantly; kāma-payo-nidhim — the ocean of love's desire; mṛga-dṛśām — of the doe-eyed; udbhāvayan — raising up (gloss: increasing); nirbharam — to the full; cetaḥ-kairava-kānanāni — the forests of night-lilies that are hearts; yaminām — of the self-controlled (gloss: yogīs); atyantam — utterly; ullāsayan — making blossom; rakṣaḥ-koka-kulāni — the flocks of cakravākas that are the demons; śoka-vikalāni — stricken with grief; ekāntam — entirely; ākalpayan — rendering; ānandam — bliss; vitanotu — may it spread; vaḥ — your; madhu-ripoḥ — of the Enemy of Madhu; vaktra-apadeśaḥ — in the guise of the face; śaśī — the moon.

3Raising to the full the ocean of desire of the doe-eyed, making the night-lily forests that are the hearts of the self-controlled blossom utterly, and rendering the flocks of cakravaka birds that are the demons entirely stricken with grief — may the moon that appears in the guise of the face of Madhu's Enemy spread your bliss.3

Song 1 — in raga Natana.

Song 1 (4)

मृदुलमलयजपवनतरलितचिकुरपरिगतकलापकं
साचितरलितनयनमन्मथशङ्कुसंकुलचित्तसुन्दरीजनजनितकौतुकम् ।
मनसिजकेलिनन्दितमानसं
भजत मधुरिपुमिन्दुसुन्दरवल्लवीमुखलालसम् ॥ ध्रु ॥
लघुतरलितकन्धरं हसितनवसुन्दरं
गजपतिप्रतापरुद्रहृदयानुगतमनुदिनम् ।
सरसं रचयति रामानन्दराय इति चारु ॥ ४ ॥

mṛdulamalayajapavanataralitacikuraparigatakalāpakaṁ
sācitaralitanayanamanmathaśaṅkusaṁkulacittasundarījanajanitakautukam |
manasijakelinanditamānasaṁ
bhajata madhuripumindusundaravallavīmukhalālasam || dhru ||
laghutaralitakandharaṁ hasitanavasundaraṁ
gajapatipratāparudrahṛdayānugatamanudinam |
sarasaṁ racayati rāmānandarāya iti cāru || 4 ||

mṛdula-malayaja-pavana — by the gentle sandal (Malaya) breeze; taralita — stirred; cikura — whose locks; parigata-kalāpakam — encircled by the peacock crest; sāci-taralita-nayana — with sidelong tremulous eyes; manmatha-śaṅku-saṅkula-citta — whose hearts are filled with Manmatha's darts; sundarī-jana — by the beautiful women; janita-kautukam — in whom eagerness is awakened; manasija-keli-nandita-mānasam — whose mind delights in love-play; bhajata — worship; madhu-ripum — the Enemy of Madhu; indu-sundara — lovely as the moon; vallavī-mukha-lālasam — longing for the faces of the cowherd girls; laghu-taralita-kandharam — with neck lightly swaying; hasita-nava-sundaram — lovely with a fresh smile; gajapati-pratāparudra-hṛdaya-anugatam — dwelling in the heart of Gajapati Pratāparudra; anudinam — day by day; sarasam — full of rasa; racayati — composes; rāmānanda-rāya — Rāmānanda Rāya; iti — thus; cāru — charmingly.

4Worship the Enemy of Madhu, whose locks are stirred by the gentle Malaya breeze, encircled by the peacock crest; in whom eagerness has been awakened by the beauties with sidelong tremulous glances, their hearts filled with the darts of Manmatha; whose mind delights in love-play — worship the Enemy of Madhu, who longs for the moon-lovely faces of the cowherd girls. (Refrain.) Him, with neck lightly swaying, lovely with a fresh smile, who day by day dwells in the heart of Gajapati Prataparudra — thus charmingly, full of rasa, does Ramananda Raya sing.4

(At the end of the benediction.)

Stage-director. Enough of prolixity! My dear, this way, this way!

(Enter the actress.)

Actress (Prakrit). Here I am, sir. To gladden with a gracious glance the heart of the maidservant fallen at your feet — that rests with my husband alone.5

Stage-director (joyfully). May you long enjoy, lady, the pleasures of youth, dressed as befits a connoisseur.

Actress (Prakrit). For what reason has my lord called me?

Stage-director. My dear, do you not know this news of favour?

Actress (Prakrit). Now my heart is bursting with curiosity to hear it.

Stage-director. Listen, dear. Today, at the close of a spring day — when the breeze that caressed the serpents, the braids lying on the Malaya mountain, the breast of the lady of the southern quarter forsaken by the young sun, had made the separated women faint, and the consoling words of their friends, the very elixir of life for the separated, were flowing; when in the clear forest of the sky the flower of cool rays, the moon, had blossomed amid the star-buds that open ever anew like undrilled pearls, poised at the tips of the creepers that are the corners of the restless eyes of separated women gazing at it in deep envy — [I was commanded] by him whose mind, like the Milk Ocean, is fit to be the abode of Lakshmi's Beloved, who covets its matchless lustre of beauty;6 a male cuckoo skilled in tasting the juice of the mango-buds of rasa ripened from vibhava and the rest;7 whose heart is adorned with the pearls of virtues that accompany the necklace on the neck of Shri. What more need be said?

Verse 10

यन्नामापि निशम्य संनिविशते सेकन्धरः कन्दरं
भूवं(?) कलवर्गभूमितिलकः सास्रं समुद्वीक्षते ।
मेने गुर्जरभूपतिर्जरदिवारण्यं निजं पत्तनं
वातव्यग्रपयोधिपोतगमिव स्वं वेद गौडेश्वरः ॥ १० ॥

yannāmāpi niśamya saṁniviśate sekandharaḥ kandaraṁ
bhūvaṁ(?) kalavargabhūmitilakaḥ sāsraṁ samudvīkṣate |
mene gurjarabhūpatirjaradivāraṇyaṁ nijaṁ pattanaṁ
vātavyagrapayodhipotagamiva svaṁ veda gauḍeśvaraḥ || 10 ||

yan-nāma — whose name; api — even; niśamya — on hearing; saṁniviśate — retreats; sekandharaḥ — Sekandhara (Sultan Sikandar); kandaram — into a cave; kalavarga-bhūmi-tilakaḥ — the ornament of the land of Kalavarga; sa-asram — with tears; samudvīkṣate — looks about; mene — considered; gurjara-bhūpatiḥ — the king of Gurjara; jarat — old; iva — like; araṇyam — forest; nijam — his own; pattanam — city; vāta-vyagra-payodhi-pota-gam — one sailing in a ship on a storm-tossed ocean; iva — as; svam — himself; veda — knows; gauḍa-īśvaraḥ — the lord of Gauḍa.

10Hearing even his name, Sekandhara hides in a cave; the ornament of the land of Kalavarga looks about with tears; the king of Gurjara has come to regard his own capital as an old forest; the lord of Gauda knows himself to be as one aboard a ship on a storm-tossed ocean.8

Verse 11

कायव्यूहविलास ईश्वरगिरेर्द्वैतं सुधादीधिते-
र्निर्यासस्तुहिनाचलस्य यमकं क्षीराम्बुराशेरसौ ।
सारः शारदवारिदस्य किमपि स्वर्वाहिनीवारिणो
द्वैराज्यं विमलीकरोति सततं यत्कीर्तिराशिर्जगत् ॥ ११ ॥

kāyavyūhavilāsa īśvaragirerdvaitaṁ sudhādīdhite-
rniryāsastuhinācalasya yamakaṁ kṣīrāmburāśerasau |
sāraḥ śāradavāridasya kimapi svarvāhinīvāriṇo
dvairājyaṁ vimalīkaroti satataṁ yatkīrtirāśirjagat || 11 ||

kāya-vyūha-vilāsaḥ — the sport of bodily multiplication; īśvara-gireḥ — of the Lord's mountain (Kailāsa); dvaitam — a double; sudhā-dīdhiteḥ — of the nectar-rayed (moon); niryāsaḥ — the extract; tuhina-acalasya — of the Snow Mountain; yamakam — a twin; kṣīra-ambu-rāśeḥ — of the Milk Ocean; asau — this; sāraḥ — the essence; śārada-vāridasya — of the autumn cloud; kim api — a certain; svar-vāhinī-vāriṇaḥ — of the waters of the heavenly river; dvairājyam — co-sovereignty; vimalīkaroti — purifies; satatam — constantly; yat-kīrti-rāśiḥ — whose mass of fame; jagat — the world.

11Is it the play of self-multiplication of the Lord's mountain, a double of the nectar-rayed moon, the extract of the Snow Mountain, a twin of the Milk Ocean, the essence of an autumn cloud? — The mass of his fame, sharing sovereignty with the waters of the heavenly river, ceaselessly purifies the world.

Verse 12

यद्दानाम्बुकदम्बनिर्मितनदीसंश्लेषहर्षादसौ
रिङ्गत्तुङ्गतरङ्गनिस्वनमिषात्प्रस्तौति यं वारिधिः ।
नित्यप्रस्तुतसप्ततन्तुभिरभिस्यूतं मनो नाकिनां
येनैतत्प्रतिमाच्छलेन यदमी मुञ्चन्ति न प्राङ्गणम् ॥ १२ ॥

yaddānāmbukadambanirmitanadīsaṁśleṣaharṣādasau
riṅgattuṅgataraṅganisvanamiṣātprastauti yaṁ vāridhiḥ |
nityaprastutasaptatantubhirabhisyūtaṁ mano nākināṁ
yenaitatpratimācchalena yadamī muñcanti na prāṅgaṇam || 12 ||

yad-dāna-ambu-kadamba — by the masses of water of his gifts; nirmita-nadī — of the rivers formed; saṁśleṣa-harṣāt — from the joy of embracing; asau — this; riṅgat-tuṅga-taraṅga — of rolling high waves; nisvana-miṣāt — under the pretext of the roar; prastauti — praises; yam — whom; vāridhiḥ — the ocean; nitya-prastuta-sapta-tantubhiḥ — by constantly performed sacrifices; abhisyūtam — stitched fast; manaḥ — the mind; nākinām — of the gods; yena — by whom; etat — so that; pratimā-chalena — under the guise of images; yat — that; amī — they; muñcanti na — do not leave; prāṅgaṇam — the courtyard.

12Rejoicing at the embrace of the rivers formed by the streams of water poured with his gifts,9 the ocean praises him under the pretext of the roar of its rolling, towering waves; and by the sacrifices he constantly performs the minds of the gods are so stitched to him that, in the form of sacred images (pratimā), they never leave his courtyard.

By him — the Rudra of the fire of world's end to the hosts of hostile kings — by the illustrious Prataparudra I have been commanded to stage some composition concerning the feet of Sri Hari. As it was said:

Verse 14

मधुरिपुपदलीलाशालि तत्तद्गुणाढ्यं
सहृदयहृदयानां काममामोदहेतुम् ।
अभिनवकृतिमन्यच्छायया नो निबद्धं
समभिनय नटानां वर्य किंचित्प्रबन्धम् ॥ १४ ॥

madhuripupadalīlāśāli tattadguṇāḍhyaṁ
sahṛdayahṛdayānāṁ kāmamāmodahetum |
abhinavakṛtimanyacchāyayā no nibaddhaṁ
samabhinaya naṭānāṁ varya kiṁcitprabandham || 14 ||

madhu-ripu-pada-līlā-śāli — resplendent with the play of the feet of Madhu's Enemy; tat-tat-guṇa-āḍhyam — rich in all those qualities; sahṛdaya-hṛdayānām — of the hearts of the sensitive; kāmam — fully; āmoda-hetum — a cause of delight; abhinava-kṛtim — a new work; anya-chāyayā — in the shadow of another; no nibaddham — not composed; samabhinaya — stage; naṭānāṁ varya — O best of actors; kiṁcit — some; prabandham — composition.

14"O best of actors, stage some composition resplendent with the play of the feet of Madhu's Enemy, rich in those very qualities of His, a source of complete delight to the hearts of the sensitive — a new work, not composed in another's shadow."

Actress. Then tell me.

Stage-director. How is that treasure-house of learning to be honoured? For even the lord of speech, wishing to speak of him, would be at a loss. (Reflecting a moment.) Ah, I remember!

Actress (Prakrit). What is it, then?

Stage-director. The poet Sri Ramananda Raya — son of Sri Bhavananda Raya, an ocean of jewel-virtues such as serenity, whose counsels, steeped in the many maxims of policy laid down by the preceptor of the gods, made the king upright and virtuous;10 a poet whose mind is adorned by the feet of Sri Hari — has composed and offered the musical drama of Ramananda called Sri Jagannatha-vallabha, dear to Gajapati Prataparudra and adorned with all these qualities. That is what I shall stage. And the poet humbly said this:

Verse 18

न भवतु गुणगन्धोऽप्यत्र नाम प्रबन्धे
मधुरिपुपदपद्मोत्कीर्तनं नस्तथापि ।
सहृदयहृदयस्यानन्दसंदोहहेतु-
र्नियतमिदमतोऽयं निष्फलो न प्रयासः ॥ १८ ॥

na bhavatu guṇagandho'pyatra nāma prabandhe
madhuripupadapadmotkīrtanaṁ nastathāpi |
sahṛdayahṛdayasyānandasaṁdohahetu-
rniyatamidamato'yaṁ niṣphalo na prayāsaḥ || 18 ||

na bhavatu — let there not be; guṇa-gandhaḥ — even a whiff of merit; api — even; atra — in this; nāma — so-called; prabandhe — composition; madhu-ripu-pada-padma — of the lotus feet of Madhu's Enemy; utkīrtanam — the glorification; naḥ — ours; tathāpi — still; sahṛdaya-hṛdayasya — of the connoisseur's heart; ānanda-saṁdoha-hetuḥ — a cause of a flood of bliss; niyatam — certainly; idam — this; ataḥ — therefore; ayam — this; niṣphalaḥ na — not fruitless; prayāsaḥ — effort.

18"Let there be not even a whiff of merit in this so-called composition — still, it is our glorification of the lotus feet of Madhu's Enemy. That will surely be the cause of a flood of bliss for the connoisseur's heart; therefore this effort is not fruitless."

So let the musicians be told to take up their vinas.

Actress (using Sanskrit). As my lord commands. (Looking ahead.) Look, look!

Verse 19

मृदुलमलयवाताचान्तवीचिप्रचारे
सरसि नवपरागैः पिञ्जरोऽयं क्लमेन ।
प्रतिकमलमधूनीपानमत्तो द्विरेफः
स्वपिति कमलकोषे निश्चलाङ्गः प्रदोषे ॥ [१९]

mṛdulamalayavātācāntavīcipracāre
sarasi navaparāgaiḥ piñjaro'yaṁ klamena |
pratikamalamadhūnīpānamatto dvirephaḥ
svapiti kamalakoṣe niścalāṅgaḥ pradoṣe || [19]

mṛdula-malaya-vāta — by the gentle Malaya breeze; ācānta-vīci-pracāre — where the play of the ripples is sipped away; sarasi — in the lake; nava-parāgaiḥ — with fresh pollen; piñjaraḥ — yellowed; ayam — this; klamena — from fatigue; prati-kamala-madhūnī-pāna-mattaḥ — drunk from drinking the honey of every lotus; dvirephaḥ — bee; svapiti — sleeps; kamala-koṣe — in the lotus cup; niścala-aṅgaḥ — with motionless limbs; pradoṣe — at evening.

19On the lake whose ripples the gentle Malaya breeze has smoothed, this bee, yellowed with fresh pollen and drunk with the honey of every lotus, sleeps at evening from fatigue in a lotus cup, its limbs motionless.11

Stage-director (joyfully). Excellent, excellent, my dear! You have cast my mind into the whirlpool of an ocean of curiosity — for you have reminded me of Narayana in yellow garments, languid with the fatigue of play full of drinking the honey of the lips of hundreds of cowherd maidens, sleeping somewhere on the couch of a heart adorned with the pillow of a mature young wife's breast.12

Behind the scenes:

Verse 21

द्वात्रिंशल्लक्षणैर्युक्तो देवदेवेश्वरो हरिः ।
गोपालबालकैः सार्धं जगाम यमुनावनम् ॥ २१ ॥

dvātriṁśallakṣaṇairyukto devadeveśvaro hariḥ |
gopālabālakaiḥ sārdhaṁ jagāma yamunāvanam || 21 ||

dvātriṁśal-lakṣaṇaiḥ — with the thirty-two marks (of a great personality); yuktaḥ — endowed; deva-deva-īśvaraḥ — the Lord of the God of gods; hariḥ — Hari; gopāla-bālakaiḥ — with the cowherd boys; sārdham — together; jagāma — went; yamunā-vanam — to the forest by the Yamunā.

21Hari, Lord of the God of gods, endowed with the thirty-two marks, has gone with the cowherd boys to the forest by the Yamuna.

Song 2 — in raga Kedara.

Song 2 (22)

मृदुतरमारुतवेल्लितपल्लववल्लीवलितशिखण्डं
तिलकविडम्बितमरकतमणितलबिम्बितशशधरखण्डम् ।
युवतिमनोहरवेशं
कलय कलानिधिमिव धरणीमनु परिणतरूपविशेषम् ॥ ध्रु ॥
खेलादोलायितमणिकुण्डलरुचिरुचिराननशोभं
हेलातरलितमधुरविलोचनजनितवधूजनलोभम् ॥
गजपतिरुद्रनराधिपचेतसि जनयतु मुदमनुवारं
रामानन्दरायकविभणितं मधुरिपुरूपमुदारम् ॥ २२ ॥

mṛdutaramārutavellitapallavavallīvalitaśikhaṇḍaṁ
tilakaviḍambitamarakatamaṇitalabimbitaśaśadharakhaṇḍam |
yuvatimanoharaveśaṁ
kalaya kalānidhimiva dharaṇīmanu pariṇatarūpaviśeṣam || dhru ||
khelādolāyitamaṇikuṇḍalarucirucirānanaśobhaṁ
helātaralitamadhuravilocanajanitavadhūjanalobham ||
gajapatirudranarādhipacetasi janayatu mudamanuvāraṁ
rāmānandarāyakavibhaṇitaṁ madhuripurūpamudāram || 22 ||

Notes

  1. Verses 1–3 and Song 4 form the nandi, the benediction opening a drama. Tribhaṅga: Krishna stands with His body bent in three places (neck, waist and knee). Above the Hindi translation of this page the 1901 editor printed "Śrī Gaurāṅga-candro vijayate" ("May Sri Gauranga-chandra be victorious"); these words are not part of the Sanskrit text of the drama.
  2. The figure apahnuti ("denial"): the thing named is denied and replaced by the object of comparison (smile → moon, eye → lotus, ear → Kama's bowstring). In their joyous bewilderment the gopis can hardly believe they are seeing Krishna's face and not the moon and lotuses.
  3. Here and throughout, the "desire" (kāma) of the gopis is their pure love (prema), merely called kāma. Krishnadasa Kaviraja explains in CC Adi 4.163–171 and Madhya 8.215 that the gopis' love is called "lust" although it aims only at Krishna's pleasure, and differs from worldly lust as gold from iron. The moon of Krishna's face gladdens the gopis and the ascetics (night-lilies open at moonrise) but grieves the demons, as moonrise grieves the cakravaka birds, which by tradition are parted at night.
  4. The closing line of the song (bhaṇitā) names the author and dedicates the song to the king. Krishna "dwelling in the heart" of Prataparudra points to the king's devotion. The phrase about "sidelong tremulous glances" is referred by the edition's footnote gloss to the beauties, not to Krishna, and is so translated.
  5. Prakrit: by the convention of Sanskrit drama, women, servants and the jester speak Prakrit. These speeches are translated from the Prakrit with the help of the Sanskrit chāyā (rendering) printed in the 1901 edition; they are marked (Prakrit).
  6. The king's mind is compared to the Milk Ocean, the abode of Vishnu, Lakshmi's Beloved. This long clause has no main verb of its own; the verb "I was commanded" comes in the speech after verse 12. The right edge of page 6 of the edition is torn; three or four letters have been restored from the sense.
  7. Vibhava, anubhava, etc. — the components of rasa in poetics; the king is called a connoisseur of rasa.
  8. A eulogy of the king (praśasti). Sekandhara is probably Sultan Sikandar (Lodi) of Delhi, with a pun on kandara, "cave". Kalavarga is Gulbarga (the Bahmani sultanate), Gurjara is Gujarat, Gauda is Bengal. The beginning of the second line is corrupt in the edition (one syllable too many for the metre) and is rendered by the sense.
  9. "Waters of his gifts": by rite a gift is accompanied by a libation of water.
  10. Bhavananda Raya was Ramananda's father; in CC Madhya 10 Mahaprabhu receives him and his sons in Puri. The Sanskrit is partly corrupt here (printed "…mantrā ṛvīkṛta…") and is rendered by the sense. The compound also admits another reading, in which Bhavananda himself is called "lord of the earth" (pṛthvīśvara), that is, a ruler.
  11. The verse is printed without a number and belongs to passage 19. The bee wearied with the honey of all the lotuses is a veiled image of Krishna wearied by His play with the gopis; so the stage-director understands it in his next speech.
  12. Narayana is here a name of Krishna. The images of Krishna's love-play with the gopis in this drama describe the transcendental (aprākṛta) rasa, the eternal play of the Lord with His own pleasure-potency, which cannot be compared to worldly lust (cf. CC Madhya 8.137: in Vrindavana Krishna is the "transcendental ever-fresh Cupid").
  13. By stage convention the stage-director calls the actor playing Krishna his "younger brother".
  14. The creepers and trees are pictured as pairs of lovers: shoots are hands, flowers are eyes, bees are collyrium. Utkalikā means both "bud" and "longing".
  15. The jester (vidūṣaka, a brahmin buffoon, the hero's friend) is a glutton and a simpleton, as the convention of Sanskrit drama requires. His name here is Ratikandala. Śikhariṇī is spiced sweet curd, rasālā a spiced drink.
  16. The sense of divocita-khelam is uncertain ("with antics fit for heaven" or "fit for the day"); Krishna teases His jester friend, at whose appearance the flowers seem to laugh.
  17. "Love" is manoja (literally "mind-born", a name of Kama). For Radha it is prema, the highest love for Krishna, not worldly passion (CC Adi 4.163–171).
  18. That is, "you know it yourself".
  19. Madanika is a friend of Radha. The Forest-goddess (Vana-devatā) is, in the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition, a name for Vrindadevi.
  20. The Five-arrowed is Kama (Cupid). In the Gaudiya Vaishnava understanding Krishna is the "transcendental Cupid" (CC Madhya 8.137), and what is described are the symptoms of loving agitation (sāttvika-bhāva) in His eternal beloveds. This is not worldly passion.
  21. Radha's face is incomparable: the lotus and the moon are not its equals, and yet poets have nothing else to compare it with.
  22. The sun, halted at the zenith, seems to scold the horses of its chariot. Kara means both "ray" and "hand". At midday the cowherd girls go home.
  23. The jester's joke draws on the Puranic story that Vishvakarma trimmed the sun on a lathe to lessen its heat.
